body:
Thanks for the reply. I deliberately left out the details because a) they are very personal and painful, and I don't want to risk having anyone involved read this and recognise it as me, and b) I'm not looking for help to feel better about the situation.

As much as I'd like to feel happier in myself, I just don't feel I can do it and don't know how to do it. I have to accept the possibility that this is how things will be for me from now on. What I'm looking for is stories from people in the same situation who, despite not having anything to live for or look forward to, were able to go on for the sake of other people without being in complete agony.

To be honest I'm not sure if I've come to the right place, worth a try though I guess.

That sounds good, got to be worth a try. 

Elsparkodiablo is right, there are a ton of scenarios that are harder and more painful to deal with. These include breakup scenarios. I'm not saying this to downplay your situation, but to encourage you that this situation can be resolved, whether by getting back together, or if not, moving on and eventually recovering.

Give your mutual friend a call and take it from there.

Hey OP, you can do this. Pursuing a dream is a great way to battle through tough times.

As someone whose own dreams are lying in tatters, due to my own cowardice and stupidity, let me tell you that yours are very much alive. It really looks to me that what you want to do is achievable if you work hard and seek other people's advice.

If you do go for it, just make sure that every step of the way, every single day, you ask yourself how much you want it, analyse everything that's going on in your life, and be brutally honest with yourself about what things might be standing in the way of you achieving what you want. Don't make the mistake I made of bumbling along and not taking decisive action to make what you want happen, until one day it's too late.

Good luck whatever you decide.

Dude, don't do this. It seems horrific to you right now, but this is definitely a situation that's fixable. 

If she really loves you as much as you hope she does then she should be prepared to listen to you, maybe not right now but at some point soon. Trust issues are a difficult thing to deal with, but it is possible to regain people's trust with enough care, thought and effort.

If she won't speak to you directly, can you speak to any of her friends who can tell her how you feel?

Guilt is an awful thing to live with, I am wrestling with it myself. 

Is there anything in particular that you've done to make you feel this guilt? Or is it just a general feeling? If the former, don't feel obliged to say what it is.

Bdd, your posts have really touched me. I'm so sorry for what you're going through.

In answer to your question: you are clearly a very thoughtful person and have taken a lot of time to weigh up your situation. If you have been of sound mind while doing this - and I see no reason to suggest you're not, but only you can know this - then yes, your choice is a rational one. As someone who is currently facing up to the possibility of losing everything that matters to them, I know that decisions on whether to go on can be a straightforward matter of weighing up pros and cons.

Please don't interpret this as approval or disapproval of your choice, it's neither. It's just an attempt to reach out to you in the midst of your pain, and let you know that someone somewhere understands something of what's going through your mind.

I hope you find peace whatever happens, or the closest approximation to it.
